newsitem.title: VIETNAM: African coffee producers appeal to Vietnam on ACPC.
newsitem.headline: African coffee producers appeal to Vietnam on ACPC.

text.p: African coffee nations will present an appeal to the president of Vietnam for Hanoi to join the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC), a senior African official said on Tuesday.

"We have a message to the president of Vietnam trying to see if they can join the ACPC," Abel Rwendeire, Minister of State for Trade and Industry for Uganda, told Reuters in an interview at the Asia Coffee Conference here.
"We'd like to appeal to the president of Vietnam so they can join," he added.

Rwendeire said the chairman of the InterAfrican Coffee Organisation (IACO), Ivory Coast commodities minister Guy-Alain Gauze, will fly to Hanoi after the conference ends this week to present the producers' letter to Vietnam's leaders.
Vietnam is Asia's second largest robusta coffee producer after Indonesia, but unlike its Southeast Asian neighbour is not a member of the ACPC and has previously resisted joining the association.
In November, Gauze blamed sales by non-ACPC members for instability in world robusta coffee prices.
The IACO has tabled a proposal ahead of a crucial ACPC meeting in Brazil next week to trim coffee exports in the first half of the year by up to 2.5 million 60 kg bags.
In mid-December, Paian Nainggolan, Indonesia's government representative to the ACPC told Reuters his country would not back the Africans' efforts to bolster prices by cutting exports.
"If we restrain our supplies, there are free riders in the region who will take over our market (share)," he said.
